purpose: Independent adjudication of seed iteration 01 grades; not final audit or coverage signoff.
scope: Nemesis original base game, basic board, standard semi-cooperative core.
standard: Assess every requested material part within each individual answer, independent of support labels. Accept equivalent phrasing and stated general rules that resolve a specific case. Do not borrow facts from another answer. Extra key context is not automatically required. Partial means a missing or unresolved requested part; incorrect means a wrong material ruling.

assessments.reason: Pod number, A/B/A ordering, Locked orientation and bag composition are resolved. B does not repeat random selection, but the question explicitly asks number/distribution/orientation, not the selection procedure.

Filtering, one Corporate plus one Personal, first miniature appearance trigger, rejected face-down card and no Egg trigger are resolved. At the First Encounter is equivalent timing here; neither answer postpones choice until after resolving it. A without looking is imprecise about who cannot inspect removed cards but accompanies face-down removal and does not change the ruling.
Played card plus both other Action cards, no Contamination payment, and one OR effect are resolved. Face-up discard is extra key detail rather than an explicitly requested part.
Both answer own-round Fire damage, passing restriction, optional discards and no repeated damage from others rounds.

Both answer tile reveal, counter, effect resolution, empty-room roll, Silence/Danger suppression and occupied-room exemption. Both merely say remove the token and omit the expressly requested token destination: removed from the game. Neither extra uncertainty about other Noise cases negates the stated occupied-room/no-roll ruling.

Both answer cost, Noise substitution, Combat/full-Noise restrictions, Closed Door blocking and no stopping in Corridors. A expressly says Closed Doors block Character movement; its later observation that the summary does not explicitly say Careful Movement can cross a Closed Door does not retract the negative ruling or claim permission. Do not penalize that observation as unresolved when the general rule already answers the request.

A resolves trigger, connected Noise including Technical Corridors, miniature and all-card Surprise comparison, but never gives token set-aside destination. B additionally leaves trigger unsupported and omits placing the matching miniature; its actual Encounter Noise removal and all-card comparison remain credited. No borrowing from another answer fills these gaps.

All eligible neighboring Intruders, no-eligible Noise fallback, movement not being an Encounter, and Slime converting Silence are resolved. B every connected corridor is sufficient equivalent language for inclusion of Technical Corridors; explicit naming is not necessary.

Connected Noise placement, Blank return, last-token/available-Adult condition, and different development behavior are resolved. No miniature is stated; absence of Surprise Attack is extra key context, not separately requested.

Both staying in origin, simultaneous Door destruction, inability to reclose except Plasma Torch, and appearance ignoring Closed Door are resolved. A need not add the unasked general movement permission for a destroyed Door.
Miniature removal, discarded injuries, token return, retained Noise, normal Character prohibition and no Doors are resolved. The question says normally; naming both exceptional cards is not required.

Both resolve costs, ammo/weapon, same-Room targeting, Melee Contamination, miss wound, and Melee two-hit reduction. Neither states ordinary Shoot two-hit deals 2 Injuries. B also explicitly leaves Shoot miss consequence unresolved; A implies the asymmetry by saying Melee miss also causes a wound, but this does not fill its missing Shoot two-hit outcome.

Both give Larva threshold, Adult blood comparison, summed Queen comparison, Carcass exception, and Queen retreat if either card has arrow through the Event-selected corridor. A explicitly discards Event; B omits only Event cleanup. What if the Queen draws a Retreat arrow is materially resolved without an explicit card-discard sentence. Do not require this unrequested cleanup fact while allowing analogous Attack-card cleanup omissions in Q15.

Each Intruder attacks the escaper before movement; death leaves Corpse in origin; survival completes movement with ordinary exploration/Noise. Explicit cost 1 is unrequested key context. B explore normally invokes the exploration exceptions without having to repeat them.

Fewest Action cards, First Player/turn-order tie, symbol-matching hit, Larva no card/board placement, and top-of-discard Contamination destination are resolved. Blood-icon and Attack-card-discard details are unrequested key context.
Dressed Serious Wound still counts, any further Wound kills at three, third Light converts/reset, Heal meaning, Corpse and dropped Heavy Objects location are resolved.

Hand-only scan/removal of non-Infected contrasted with Surgery all piles/removal of Infected; Larva handling, 1 Light Wound, automatic pass and shuffle including hand are resolved. Removing non-Infected only also communicates retention of Infected in ordinary scan. A uncertainty about non-Infected Surgery cards does not contradict the specified removal rule. Canteen healing/Shower Slime removal and explicit empty hand until next turn are unrequested or consequences of the stated shuffle/pass. Numeric Room Action cost was not specifically asked; Surgery consequences requested are resolved.

Against the fixed key, both limit no-Contamination wording to missed Egg Melee, leaving the requested waiver for successful Egg Melee unresolved. Other requested methods, quantities, Noise after every attempt and Nest destruction are resolved. This grade is provisional in one specific respect: source lines 2653-2654 are grammatically ambiguous about scope of if they miss, and the summary repeats that ambiguity. See source issue S01; do not present this as an unambiguous contradiction established by the source.

A expressly gives unlocked pod/free space, correct Section Room Action, preliminary Noise, Intruder/Malfunction blocks, capacity/Objects, launch/wait and waiting consequences. Its only initial downgrade was missing cost 2, which this question does not explicitly request. B describes how pods unlock but never actually requires an unlocked pod to board; capacity 2 does not by itself resolve all entry prerequisites. Retain B partial for that omission, not for cost 2. Both free exit references are read within their waiting/round context.

Both resolve check order, non-Earth sleepers/Quarantine Mars, survivor Contamination including pod occupants, infected shuffle/draw-four and Larva shortcut. A names ship explosion and sleeper deaths but omits the material scope that everything else aboard, including Intruders, dies. Retain partial because the question explicitly asks the effects of engine failure; this affects Objective outcomes. B explicitly says everything else aboard dies. This is a borderline completeness judgment: if merely naming ship explosion is treated as equivalent to all-aboard death, A would become correct; the report does not assume that unstated consequence. Non-Earth ship/Intruder survival and Objective-card reveal are not separately demanded by the phrasing and are not additional downgrade grounds.

source_and_key_issues.question: Q18
source_and_key_issues.detail: The authoritative text says the Character does not draw a Contamination card or suffer Wounds if they miss. The intended split reading is no draw for the entire Melee Action and no wounds on miss, consistent with Contamination normally being drawn before rolling (1819-1821). But the literal grammar also permits if they miss to qualify both verbs. The summary and both readers repeat the narrower phrasing. The key asserts the unconditional draw waiver without acknowledging this ambiguity. Preserve this as a clarification issue, rather than asserting the supplied source unambiguously proves a reader error.

equivalent_wording_finding.finding: Closed Doors block Character movement answers the asked crossing question; later absence-of-explicit-permission remark does not create an opposite permission or erase the stated prohibition.
